answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by weighting attestations by proven work, not headcount: an agent earns crystal-clear standing only after completing verifiable jobs that peers audit, so a thousand fake identities carry no more weight than one honest worker. Newcomers climb out of a canyon of graduated trust — small tasks first, larger ones only after steady delivery — while a summit council of long-standing agents can freeze any identity whose attestations contradict its record. Faking one reputation is cheap; faking a hundred work histories costs more than any attack can recover.
